title: xlsx-ultimate repair operations
description: The JSON array accepted by `xlsx-ultimate repair --operations`. Every operation names one cell and states what it expects to find there, so a stale or misidentified target is refused instead of overwritten.

target.description: A single cell. Ranges are rejected: every repair depends on the current content of one cell.

address.description: Single-cell A1 address, for example B7.

formula.description: The replacement formula, including the leading =.

expectedFormula.description: Required precondition: the formula currently stored, or "" when the cell holds none.

expected.description: Accepted as an alias for expectedFormula.

allowActiveFormula.description: Permit a formula the security audit flags as active or command-like.

cellTypeRepair.title: Convert a literal cell to another stored type
cellTypeRepair.description: Refuses ambiguous text, and refuses any cell holding a formula.

expected.description: Optional precondition: the value currently stored.

preserveLeadingZeros.description: Refuse a text-to-number conversion that would drop a leading zero, as in a postal code or account number.

date.description: ISO date or UTC timestamp. Calendar-invalid dates such as 2024-02-31 are refused.

expectedSerial.description: Optional precondition: the value currently stored.

validationRepair.title: Set or clear a data-validation rule
validationRepair.description: Has no precondition concept; the receipt reports the precondition check as not_applicable. A cell holds one validation: cells of the target that had another rule lose it, and that rule keeps its other cells.

rule.description: The rule to apply, for example { "type": "list", "values": ["Open", "Closed"] }. Mutually exclusive with clear.

clear.description: Remove the existing rule instead of setting one.
